summary: Rebecca Rowena Randall, a poor girl selling soap and cakes door to door, pitches her product to a wealthy stranger on a porch and describes the Simpson family's need for a banquet lamp. The man, amused and generous, orders three hundred cakes so the Simpsons can afford the lamp and a shade. Rebecca tips into lilac bushes in surprise, then gives her name and guesses the buyer is Mr. Aladdin, after which she runs to tell Emma Jane the good news.
one_line: A peddler girl named Rebecca wins a large order from a generous stranger to help the Simpson family buy a banquet lamp.
key_facts: Rebecca tells the man that she lives with her aunts in a brick house and that her aunts would not like her to be a peddler.
Rebecca describes the Simpson family's poverty, joyless life, and need of a banquet lamp to brighten their existence.
The man says he has known what it was to do without a banquet lamp.
Rebecca estimates that if the Simpsons sell two hundred more cakes this month and next, they can have the lamp by Christmas.
Rebecca says they could get a shade by summer time, but she cannot help much after today because her aunt Miranda may not like it.
The man agrees to take three hundred cakes, which will give the Simpsons the shade and all.
Rebecca tips over on her stool and disappears into a clump of lilac bushes after hearing the large order.
The man tells Rebecca she should have replied 'Can't you make it three hundred and fifty?' instead of capsizing.
Rebecca gives her full name as Rebecca Rowena Randall.
The man remarks 'BOTH? Your mother was generous' about Rebecca's two given names.
Rebecca says her mother could not bear to give up either of the names.
Rebecca guesses the man must be Mr. Aladdin in the Arabian Nights.
Rebecca runs down the lane to tell Emma Jane, who has been waiting and must be tired.
